The base identifies the input document, not the source of the updated policy. Homelab owns private shared rules and repository membership; Janitor publishes its working-document and public-source rules.

The owner-approved standing merge policy is already implemented in [Janitor #182](https://github.com/Khamel83/janitor/pull/182); [#184](https://github.com/Khamel83/janitor/pull/184) adds draft promotion. Every PR type in Homelab's active, nonexcluded scope qualifies after the latest trusted OCI bot PASS at its exact current head. GitHub's normal SHA-pinned merge endpoint enforces required checks and branch protections. This projection grants no new authority to create or deploy changes.

## Repair evidence

The owner explicitly reconfirmed the standing all-PR exact-head PASS merge authorization in this Janitor backlog task. This existing proposal now uses the current published working-docs contract and correct public/private profile. Render idempotence, valid managed sentinels, byte-identical project text outside those blocks, and `git diff --check` pass. No runtime or deployment changed.

## Explicit approved policy change

This intentionally projects the owner's standing PASS merge decision, replacing the obsolete documentation-only paragraph. The owner explicitly instructed: “I meant every PR with a bot pass would merge.” The owner assigned active-repository membership and explicit exclusions to Homelab, and separately assigned reviewer/PASS improvements to Homelab while Janitor continuously checks and merges eligible results. The owner then authorized completion: “This is approved. I want it completed. You have whatever approval you need to get this done.” This owner decision is supplied directly here; the private implementation links are historical provenance, not evidence the reviewer must fetch to discover the decision.

The broadening of PR-type eligibility and removal of the old author/path/label restrictions are the expressly approved behavior, not accidental changes. Adding a per-PR human approval or an optional-CI gate would contradict that decision. GitHub's normal SHA-pinned merge endpoint still enforces every configured required check and branch protection. A trusted PASS grants standing authority to merge an existing eligible proposal; it does not itself authorize creating unrelated changes or deploying them.

The standing worker obtains current active membership and explicit per-repository `pr_auto_merge: false` exclusions from Homelab's authoritative project catalog, and fails closed when that source is invalid. Project repositories are row-scoped projections and intentionally do not copy the private fleet catalog or its exclusion list. Homelab owns the reviewer and PASS process; Janitor owns execution of the approved merge rule. This change does not grant an arbitrary repository agent the worker's credentials or make that agent the scope authority.

The title explicitly calls out the approved standing PASS policy. This clarification changes metadata only; the reviewed source head is unchanged.

## Recommendation

This is a proposal for evaluation. It does not mean that implementation, approval, deployment, or adoption has occurred.

**Capability:** A Markdown-based agent skill that rewrites AI-sounding prose to read more naturally while preserving its meaning and optionally matching a supplied writing sample.
**Confidence:** 0.86

## Starred repository evidence

- **Repository:** [blader/humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer)
- **Description:** Agent skill that removes signs of AI-generated writing from text
- **Latest observed commit:** 9862685f575c65a8247f90369951df1b3416e3d6

## Matched repository evidence

- **Repository:** [Khamel83/TrojanHorse](https://github.com/Khamel83/TrojanHorse)
- **Description:** No description
- **Recent commits in window:** 92
- **Target subsystem:** `The documentation-generation workflow defined by the `doc_draft` task class in `AGENTS.md`, producing repository prose such as `README.md`, `API_DOCUMENTATION.md`, `WORKFLOWS.md`, and operational documentation.`

## Direct relationship

Install Humanizer as a project-local agent skill for the agents used by the `doc_draft` lane, then add an explicit Humanizer revision step after drafting and before review or commit. The source README documents project-local installation, agent selection, direct text input, and file-path rewriting; the target already defines skill-aware agent workflows and a dedicated documentation-drafting route.

Supporting evidence:
- The source capability is implemented as Markdown and states that it works with any agent supporting skills, avoiding a Python runtime or package integration requirement.
- The source documents project-local installation without `--global` and supports selecting a particular agent or all agents with `--agent`.
- The source accepts a repository file path directly, exemplified by humanizing prose in a documentation file.
- The target `AGENTS.md` defines a concrete `doc_draft` task class routed to writing-capable agents, providing a specific workflow insertion point.
- The target `CLAUDE.md` explicitly describes a skills-based operating model, indicating compatibility with an agent skill rather than requiring changes to the corpus-processing engine.
- The target safe-file inventory contains several prose-heavy documentation targets, including `README.md`, `API_DOCUMENTATION.md`, `WORKFLOWS.md`, `TESTING_GUIDE.md`, and `LLM-OVERVIEW.md`.
- The source has recent maintenance focused on awkward phrasing, pattern accuracy, claim preservation, inline-code protection, and package validation.

## Expected benefit

Documentation produced by the existing `doc_draft` workflow can receive a repeatable prose-quality pass that reduces formulaic AI phrasing without adding runtime dependencies or touching the local evidence ingestion, normalization, RAG, or API subsystems.

## Proposed implementation outline

1. Install `blader/humanizer` locally for the agent or agents assigned to `doc_draft`; do not install it as an application dependency in `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt`.
1. Update the `doc_draft` workflow instructions in `AGENTS.md` so Humanizer runs only after the factual draft is complete and before the existing review and commit stages.
1. Constrain invocation to prose sections in named documentation files and exclude code blocks, commands, paths, configuration keys, API identifiers, quoted evidence, and machine-generated corpus artifacts.
1. Provide a short sample of the owner's accepted documentation prose when voice matching is desired.
1. Review the resulting diff for changed technical meaning, weakened requirements, altered rankings or simultaneity claims, and damage to inline code before accepting it.

## Compatibility and risks

High at the workflow level: Humanizer is a Markdown agent skill, the target explicitly uses skills and agent-routed documentation tasks, and no target runtime dependency is required. Compatibility is not established for embedding Humanizer inside the Python corpus engine, so integration should remain an authoring-time agent step.

- A stylistic rewrite could subtly alter technical requirements, provenance statements, scope boundaries, or operational instructions despite the source's meaning-preservation goal.
- Applying it to corpus evidence or generated reports could modify source-backed material and conflict with the target's deterministic, local evidence-archive purpose.
- Unrestricted file rewriting could alter code blocks, commands, identifiers, or structured Markdown; the integration must be limited to prose and reviewed as a diff.
- The supplied evidence does not expose the target dispatch implementation files, so automating the step inside `core.dispatch` would require additional repository evidence; the supported seam is the documented `AGENTS.md` workflow.

- The target subsystem has a focused test.
- The integration preserves the target repository's existing behavior.

## Recommendation

**Capability:** Plan-scoped subagent-driven development with durable progress state, resume-based review/fix rounds, scoped re-review, and a bounded five-round breaker.

## Starred repository evidence

- **Repository:** [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)
- **Description:** An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
- **Latest observed commit:** b36e0829c6d0140e93cfef2ca599b1b07d4a7797

## Direct relationship

Extend each ONE_SHOT implementation plan and dispatch manifest with a stable plan identifier and plan-scoped execution state. The /full build loop can resume only that plan's pending dispatches, record review findings by task, request scoped re-review after fixes, and stop or escalate after a bounded number of unsuccessful rounds.

Supporting evidence:
- The source README describes a workflow that turns an approved design into an implementation plan and executes it through subagent-driven development with testing discipline.
- Source commit b8a2d84b40a33d7e047f2267ade109a67a2e19c0 adds plan-scoped durable progress where the ledger names its plan and the workspace ends with that plan.
- Source commit 6df8ba145873f72d3307f128745c7aea00f589c4 adds one isolated .superpowers/sdd/<plan> workspace per plan.
- Source commits ebdd4ec61f2f560bada4f6ded7b0806e62bf33f7 and 87e4050daac906590f6002ba90e0c587ebf6a2fe add a resume-based fix loop, five-round breaker, rationalization table, and scoped re-review prompt.
- The target AGENTS.md already defines phase-based planning, parallel worker dispatch, structured output capture, manifest validation, context checkpoints, and a loop until the goal is met, providing a direct orchestration seam rather than a generic dependency overlap.
- The target README already treats docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-local-work-corpus-design.md and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-04-local-work-corpus-implementation.md as authoritative project documents, demonstrating an existing compatible plan/spec namespace.
- The target has 92 commits in the activity window and a current 2026-09-09 push, making workflow integration relevant to active development rather than a dormant repository.

## Expected benefit

Make interrupted or review-heavy ONE_SHOT executions reliably resumable without mixing state across plans, while preventing unbounded worker-review-fix cycles and reducing repeated cross-plan forensic work.

## Proposed implementation outline

1. Define a stable plan slug or identifier for every /full implementation plan and include it in each 1shot/dispatch manifest.
1. Create a plan-scoped state location associated with the existing docs/superpowers/plans namespace, recording task status, worker output, validation result, review findings, and fix-round count.
1. Update the AGENTS.md /full and dispatch protocols so resume operations load only the ledger belonging to the selected plan and reject stale or mismatched state.
1. After a failed review, dispatch fixes only for recorded findings and run a scoped re-review of those findings instead of repeating the complete review.
1. Add a bounded round counter modeled on the source's five-round breaker; escalate unresolved findings rather than looping indefinitely.
1. Terminate or archive the plan-scoped workspace when all plan tasks and verification gates complete, while retaining the normal dispatch manifests as execution evidence.

## Compatibility and risks

High at the workflow layer. The source capability is an agent methodology implemented around composable skills and shell-oriented tooling, while the target's product is Python; integration belongs in AGENTS.md and the dispatch/plan state machinery rather than in the work-corpus Python package. The target already uses Superpowers-style spec and plan paths and already has the required concepts of plans, subagents, manifests, validation, and iterative completion.

- The target already has context checkpoints, handoff behavior, TaskList state, and dispatch manifests; adding another state authority without a clear precedence rule could create conflicting progress records.
- A five-round breaker must escalate actionable diagnostics rather than silently treating the plan as complete.
- Plan identifiers and cleanup rules must prevent a resumed run from consuming stale manifests belonging to another plan.

## Acceptance criteria

- The target subsystem has a focused test.
- The integration preserves the target repository's existing behavior.
